thread:
sara: Heads up — customer cust-842 (Dedicated) hitting intermittent 502s + latency spikes during the canary rollout. Seeing reqids: abc123, def456, ghi789. Can we collect repro artifacts and confirm whether pin/fallback happened? :eyes:

mike: Got it. Please grab the `x-request-id` header values and any `trace-id`s. If you can run a curl repro that would help — also collect a debug bundle from the node that served the requests.

alex: Quick curl template you can paste:```bash
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" 
     -H "x-request-id: abc123" 
     -H "x-customer-id: cust-842" 
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
     -d '{"model":"gpt-small","input":"short prompt"}' 
     https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
```Use `-H \"x-redwood-version: canary\"` to force canary and omit it for stable.

infra-bot: deploy-event: {"env":"prod","service":"runtime","change":"canary-swap","version":"canary-2026-03-12","ts":"1967889000"} :information_source:

eng-ml: When you capture the debug bundle, please include kernel logs and the model binary checksum. For model pin question: send the `model` header we used in the request — if it was pinned it should show `gpt-small@stable-2026-03-01` vs `gpt-small@canary-2026-03-12`.

sara: I collected two curl runs (stable + canary) and uploaded a debug bundle to s3://redwood-debug/cust-842/1967890123-debug.tar.gz. Bundle contains the request logs, node stdout, and `/var/log/redwood/kvcache.log`. Links attached.

support-bot: debug-bundle uploaded: https://s3.console.aws.amazon.com/s3/object/redwood-debug/cust-842/1967890123-debug.tar.gz :white_check_mark:

mike: Thanks — I'll pull the bundle. If you can also forward the exact timestamps for abc123 and def456 I can correlate with the gateway traces. Did the customer observe fallback responses that returned from the stable replica? Any `x-redwood-fallback` header?

sara: abc123 at 2026-03-12T15:22:07Z, def456 at 2026-03-12T15:22:31Z. No explicit `x-redwood-fallback` in the app logs — just 502s and some long tail latencies.

alex: I checked the gateway traces for abc123 — request routed to canary pool and we see `KV_CACHE_MISS` spike and a local OOM on that worker around the same time. Trace: https://apm.redwood/app/trace/abc123

eng-ml: OOM + KV miss could explain latency and 502s. For repro: try a looped curl with concurrency 4 to the canary header to simulate load:```bash
for i in {1..20}; do 
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" -H "x-redwood-version: canary" -H "x-request-id: test-$i" -d '{"model":"gpt-small","input":"repro prompt"}' https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate &
done
wait
```Also include `--max-time 30` to avoid waiting forever.

mike: I'll open a pinned job to run that against a canary instance and collect perf counters. If repro consistent, plan: pin customer to stable while we patch the canary kernel and then resume canary after validation.

sara: OK I'll notify the customer and request permission to pin them. Any preferred rollback wording?

alex: Keep it simple: "We're pinning your traffic to the stable model variant while we investigate an intermittent resource issue in the canary. This is temporary and won't affect your data." :thumbsup:

sara: Perfect. Thanks all — uploading the stdout excerpts and curl logs to the ticket now. Will post when pinning is complete. :pray:
